ElementDescription: The NDAR Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for research subject
Subject ID how it's defined in lab/project
Date on which the interview/genetic test/sampling/imaging/biospecimen was completed. MM/DD/YYYY
Age in months at the time of the interview/test/sampling/imaging.
Notes: Age is rounded to chronological month. If the research participant is 15-days-old at time of interview, the appropriate value would be 0 months. If the participant is 16-days-old, the value would be 1 month.
M = Male; F = Female; O=Other; NR = Not reported

ElementDescription: Free text about interviewees' experience with treatment for alcohol use disorder
Notes: For patients, experience refers to receiving treatments to help with AUD. For physicians, experience refers to prescribing medications/referring for residential treatments/delivering psychotherapy for their patients.

ElementDescription: Free text about interviewees' preference for different treatments for alcohol use disorder
Notes: For patients, preference refers to which treatment they want to use. For physicians, preference refers to which treatment they want to prescribe for their patients with alcohol use disorder.

ElementDescription: Free text about interviewees' belief of the effectiveness of different treatments for alcohol use disorder
Free text about interviewees' experience with accessing different treatments for alcohol use disorder
Notes: Patients are asked how easy it is for them to discuss treatment with providers. Providers are asked how they see their role in discussing treatment options with patients.

ElementDescription: Free text about interviewees' opinions on how useful the information of comparative effectiveness among different treatments for alcohol use disorder will be in clinical practice
Notes: Patients are asked how much the comparative effectiveness information will motivate them to quit or reduce drinking. Providers are asked how much the comparative effectiveness information will motivate them to prescribe medications or refer patients for specialty treatment.

ElementDescription: Free text about interviewees' opinions on how the information of comparative effectiveness among different treatments for alcohol use disorder should be presented
Notes: Focus is on asking how to frame the information, which format to present it, e.g. numbers, pictograms, etc.

ElementDescription: Free text about interviewees' opinions on how to make the information of comparative effectiveness among different treatments for alcohol use disorder trusted by patients and providers
Free text about interviewees' opinions on how to use the information of comparative effectiveness among different treatments for alcohol use disorder in clinical practice
Notes: For patients, focus is how to make the patients feel comfortable to discuss treatment with their providers, giving that now they have the comparative effectiveness information included in the decision aid. Providers are asked how to make it easier to use the comparative effectiveness information in clinical practice.

ElementDescription: Miscellaneous comments on study, interview, methodology relevant to this form data
